comment: Source read at commit 95496e8, HEAD of the maker's repository; its plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed 2.1.0 manifest. ES40.cpp:45-46 pack inputs 0 and 1 into the high and middle bytes of the left word and inputs 2 and 3 into the same bytes of the right, then split input 4: (b[4] << 0) & 0xf0 goes into the low byte of the left word and (b[4] << 4) & 0xf0 into the low byte of the right, so the fifth header is the only one that does not get a whole byte and the low four bits of each word are always zero. The Category menu is the same submenu as on the ES-5 Encoder, selecting 0x800000, 0x7fff80 or 0x7fffff; the maker's page does not mention it. The outputs are given no family: they carry encoded words destined for a DAC rather than audio, control voltage, pitch or a trigger. The panel prints the inputs 1 to 5 and leaves the outputs unlabelled; left and right come from the source.
